blocks.heading: Waste the Most Years and Money

items.text: Law, psychology, design, mass communication, social work, hotel management, and animation are all real routes with real hiring behind them when taken seriously.
A BJMC, BSW, or BA degree from an unranked private college with no placement cell is a different bet than the same course at a well-regarded institute.
Several of the courses on this list, especially BFA, BSW, BJMC, and animation diplomas, pay modestly at entry almost everywhere.

blocks.heading: Compare the Practical Paths
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Courses for arts students after 12th, ranked by real fit

rows: BA (major in Psychology, Economics, Political Science, English, History, Sociology)
CUET UG for most central and many state universities; direct merit at some state colleges
The most flexible route and the one arts students default to. It pays only when you pick a major deliberately and add proof of work, not because the degree name alone opens doors.
BA LLB (5-year integrated law)
CLAT UG for National Law Universities; CUET UG or private-university tests for others

A genuinely strong path when you like reading, argument, and structured thinking. The competition is two-stage: clearing CLAT is one hurdle, building a well-paying practice afterward is a separate, harder climb.
BJMC / BA in Journalism and Mass Communication
CUET UG or the institute's own entrance test; some private colleges take direct admission
Good for writing- and media-inclined students, but newsroom hiring has shrunk while digital, brand, and content roles have grown. Treat this as a base, not a guarantee of a reporting job.
BFA (Bachelor of Fine Arts) and design-adjacent UG courses
Portfolio-based entrance tests; NID and NIFT run their own separate national entrance exams
Portfolio quality matters more than the degree label. This path rewards visible work and scales well, since a strong portfolio can later grow into freelance work or a studio.
BSW (Bachelor of Social Work)
Merit-based or entrance-test admission depending on the university; CUET UG at many central universities
A genuine route into NGO, CSR, and social-sector work. Pay stays modest at entry almost everywhere, so this needs a clear-eyed view of the sector's pay ceiling before committing years to it.
BA or BSc in Psychology
CUET UG for most universities; a few private colleges run their own aptitude round

Strong when paired with genuine patience for years of further study. A bachelor's degree alone rarely qualifies you to practise clinically; the real career usually needs a master's and supervised registration.

blocks.heading: Why the Combination Pays
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Why the combination pays, not the subject alone

rows: BA English or BJMC
Content strategy plus one real published portfolio of writing samples
Newsroom hiring alone has shrunk. Writing plus digital strategy opens brand, content, and communications roles that are actually growing.
BA LLB
A specialisation through an LLM after CLAT-PG (IP, tax, or tech law)
A generalist law degree caps out faster than most students expect. Specialisation is what firms pay a premium for, not the degree alone.
BA or BSc Psychology
Research method training plus a genuine plan for a master's and supervised registration
A bachelor's in psychology alone rarely qualifies anyone to practise. The multiplier is the further study most students underestimate.
BFA or animation diploma
A finished portfolio or demo reel with three to five strong pieces
Hiring managers in design and animation filter almost entirely on portfolio quality, not institute name.

visuals.heading: Check Before Reacting to a Course Name

blocks.heading: Arts Only Really Leads to a Plain

items.text: Any BA degree is basically the same as any other BA degree.
Creative or people-facing courses like BFA or BSW "do not count" as serious courses.
A course is good simply because a relative says it worked out for someone they know.
Writing, content strategy, and basic digital marketing, using free or low-cost courses and real practice.
Design fundamentals and UX basics, before committing to a full bootcamp or design degree.
Testing genuine interest in psychology through an audited introductory course before a three-year degree.

blocks.heading: Nobody in the Family Can Describe

items.text: Ask how the student will build proof early.
Do not spend heavily on an average course if it leaves no room for tools, a portfolio, internships, or later upskilling.
Ask whether the route fits the student or only the family's comfort with the label.
